Tests for {@link QCodec}, which implements RFC 1522 "Q" encoding for non-ASCII characters in email headers. Special characters are escaped as =XX hex sequences and spaces may optionally be encoded as underscores.
"Grüezi_zämä" — a Swiss German greeting, contains Latin characters with umlauts (ü, ä)
"Всем_привет" — Russian for "Hello everyone", composed entirely of Cyrillic code points
Builds a String by casting each element of {@code unicodeChars} to a {@code char}.
'=' is unsafe and becomes =3D; CR+LF become =0D=0A
Decode a valid encoded String passed as Object
Null input must produce null output
Non-String types are unsupported and must throw DecoderException
When encodeBlanks is false, spaces are left as literal spaces in the encoded form
When encodeBlanks is true, spaces are replaced with underscores per RFC 1522
Both encoded forms must decode back to the original plain text
Encode a valid String passed as Object
Null input must produce null output
Non-String types are unsupported and must throw EncoderException
Constructing a QCodec with an unrecognised charset name must throw immediately
Verify that setEncodeBlanks / isEncodeBlanks round-trip correctly
doEncoding and doDecoding (the low-level byte-array hooks) must tolerate null gracefully
'?', '_', and '=' are all unsafe in Q encoding and must be escaped
"Всем_привет"
"Grüezi_zämä"
Verify the exact RFC 1522 encoded forms for each language
Encoding then decoding must recover the original text exactly
